Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. packages/excalidraw/tests/arrowheadSize.test.tsx > arrowhead size > choosing medium clears the size: AssertionError: expected 'large' to be undefined (line 82: expect(updated.arrowheadSize).toBeUndefined(); line 83 also requires JSON.stringify(updated) not to contain "arrowheadSize"). Cause: actionChangeArrowheadSize calls newElementWith(el, { arrowheadSize }) where normalizeArrowheadSize("medium") is undefined; newElementWith skips undefined values when detecting a change, so it returns the element unchanged. When the normalized size is undefined, the action must return a new element (version bumped, as newElementWith with force does) that does not carry the arrowheadSize key at all (e.g. destructure the key out, then newElementWith(rest, {}, true)). Keep every other behaviour of the action as is.

Fix `packages/element/src/delta.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. packages/excalidraw/tests/arrowheadSize.test.tsx > arrowhead size > undo restores the previous size: AssertionError: expected 'small' to be undefined (line 71). An arrow created without the arrowheadSize key is set to 'small' through the properties panel (CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY), then Keyboard.undo(); the element still has arrowheadSize 'small'. Undo must restore the key's absence (value undefined, ideally key removed) for an optional element property that was absent before the change. Make the smallest change in the element-delta apply/calculate path so a property whose previous value was undefined is cleared on undo (and redo sets it again), without changing behaviour for any existing property.
